melting point 174.87 °C: A semicrystalline bar cannot hold its shape above its melting point.
glass transition 59.76 °C + 20 °C: An amorphous matrix softens at its glass transition; fibres carry a bar only a little further.

45 °C floor: Heat deflection is measured by heating a loaded bar from room temperature (ISO 75, ASTM D648). A bar soft enough to deflect near room temperature has no meaningful HDT, and no filament in the snapshot measures below 48 °C even at 1.8 MPa. A soft floor, so a PE or BVOH estimate cannot reach below freezing.

polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. NatureWorks Ingeo 3D850 (R-NATUREWORKS-INGEO-3D850-TDS), a PLA grade for 3D-printing monofilament, prints a specific gravity of 1.24 (ASTM D792), a peak melt temperature of 165-180 °C and a glass transition temperature of 55-60 °C (both ASTM D3418), p. 1. It prints no water absorption. PLA is semicrystalline and prints amorphous (D158): the melting point column holds 165 °C, the low end of the printed range, a ceiling every grade of the range stays under. The same page says that annealing "in the range of 176-266°F (80-130°C) can be used to promote crystallization": the annealing threshold is the glass transition's low end, 55 °C, at or below which nothing crystallises (D158).
